text: You're out. Another QR code. On menus, posters, everywhere. A few years ago, rare. Now, ubiquitous. You just want simple, instant information.
You used to ignore them. But then, you pull out your phone, point, and click. Instantly, a menu loads, a website opens. It worked, seamlessly.
This smooth experience makes you wonder: why the sudden explosion? QR codes existed for decades. Was it a global decision, or just recent events?
The real system is simpler: friction disappeared. Modern smartphone cameras scan codes directly, no app needed. This tiny technical shift removed the biggest barrier.
The cost? Your physical world is now full of invisible doorways. Every object becomes a clickable link, making access effortless but also trackable.
Next time, you won't just see a pattern. You'll see an efficient, ubiquitous bridge – a triumph of minimal friction, connecting our world.
